comments.body:
Status note rather than a ping: the five workflows on this PR have been in `action_required` since I opened it on 14 August — Unit Testing, Linting, Core Typecheck, Build Package and CodeQL never started, so the PR shows no checks at all rather than green ones. From the outside that reads as unverified, which I suspect is why it has been quiet.

Could a maintainer press "Approve and run workflows"? So that approving is not an act of faith, here is the local run against current `main`. Nothing upstream has touched either file since I opened this, and GitHub still reports it mergeable:

```
$ pytest tests/evaluation/test_metrics.py -q
49 passed
```

With only the change to `metrics.py` reverted and the tests kept:

```
5 failed, 44 passed
```

The defect, restated briefly: `hit_rate` and `average_precision` count matches per expected id rather than per retrieved position, so a ranking that repeats a node id — which is what fusion retrievers produce — scores above 1. Measured 2.0 for hit rate and average precision and 1.63 for NDCG, which makes a mean over an eval set incomparable between runs.

Happy to rebase, split it, or drop the extra test cases if any of that helps it move.

Gentle nudge on this one and its two siblings (#22684, #22685): the workflows have been in `action_required` since 14 August and have never started, so all three show no checks rather than green ones. A maintainer pressing "Approve and run workflows" on any one of them should unblock the set.

Each is a one- or two-line fix with a regression test that fails on `main`:
- #22683 — retrieval metrics can exceed 1.0 when the same id repeats in the retrieved set
- #22684 — MMR scores each candidate only against the last selected result instead of all selected results
- #22685 — the multi-modal retrieval evaluator counts `ImageNode` as text

All three verified locally against current `main`. Happy to rebase if it helps.
Friendly ping: this is ready for review whenever someone has a moment. Happy to adjust anything.
